annotations.title: Recipes: nutrition, allergens and a shopping list

description: Never call a meal safe or healthy or say it suits a medical condition; give the numbers. You write the recipe or the week of meals; divux does the math you can't do exactly and gives the person a page: exact nutrition per serving and per day from USDA data, allergen flags, any active FDA recall on a named brand, scaling to any servings, and one shopping list that merges the same ingredient across the week and rounds up to amounts shops sell, with 'Find it' price links. Send amounts as a number and a unit (g, kg, oz, lb, ml, l, tsp, tbsp, cup, or a count like 3 for eggs), never 'a handful' or 'to taste'; send grams for anything sold or weighed oddly (a can, a branded item); name foods plainly; brand only when the person named one. For a week send days, each with meals (recipe, make = servings cooked, eat = servings one person eats, default 1); per-day nutrition is for one person. For a family send household (adults, kids' ages, allergies, foods to avoid). With a weekly budget send budget and a price_estimate on each ingredient. Send goals and diet when given. Allergen and diet flags come from ingredient names; the package label is what counts. Not medical or diet advice.

amount.description: The exact amount as a number: 1.5, or '1 1/2'. Not 'a handful' or 'to taste'.

brand.description: Only when the person named a brand, e.g. 'Cheerios': Divux then checks recent FDA recalls for it

grams.description: The weight in grams of this whole amount, when you know it (best for a can, a cup of something unusual, or a branded item). It beats any conversion.

name.description: The ingredient, e.g. 'rolled oats', 'chicken breast', 'olive oil'. Put preparation in note, not here.

per_100g.description: Nutrition per 100 g from the package, only if you have it; skips the lookup

price_estimate.description: Your estimate in USD for this amount of the ingredient, when the person gave a budget. Divux doesn't look up prices here.

query.description: What to look up for nutrition when name is not enough, e.g. 'chicken breast raw' or 'cheddar cheese'

unit.description: g, kg, oz, lb, ml, l, tsp, tbsp, cup, fl oz, or a count word (clove, slice, piece). Leave out for whole items like eggs.

note.description: A short tip or description for the top of the page

servings.description: How many servings the recipe as written makes

steps.description: The method, one step per entry, in order

budget.description: Weekly food budget in USD. With price_estimate on ingredients, Divux totals the shopping list and warns when it's over.

days.description: A week of meals, up to 21 recipes in all. Leave out when sending one recipe.

make.description: Servings cooked; default the recipe's own servings

diet.description: Diets to check the ingredients against

goals.description: The person's own targets per day; the page's bars are drawn against them instead of FDA Daily Values

household.description: Family meals: who eats. Divux scales portions per person, and flags or rejects ingredients that break an allergy or avoid.

allergies.description: Allergies in the household: milk, eggs, fish, shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, soy, sesame (or any other word, which is treated as an avoid)

avoid.description: Foods the household won't eat, e.g. 'mushrooms', 'cilantro'

kids.description: Each child's age in years, e.g. [3, 8]. Children get smaller portions by age.

strict.description: True to refuse the plan (nothing saved) when an ingredient breaks an allergy or avoid; otherwise they are flagged

recipe.description: One recipe. Leave out when sending days.

title.description: Name for a week plan, e.g. 'High-protein week'. A single recipe uses its own title.
